Subject: Re: Redwood SOW - request for staged termination/fee tranche

Jonas / Redwood team,

Attached is MedCure's annotated clause set (see attachment: MedCure-Counterterms-annotated.docx). Our procurement and legal teams remain comfortable with credits for intermittent latency degradations, but for repeated or prolonged availability failures they are requesting: a) a three-tranche fee-at-risk schedule (10% holdback on month 1, 20% on month 3, 30% on month 6) tied to rolling SLA miss thresholds; b) clear unilateral termination right after the second consecutive severity-1 incident lasting >45 minutes where credits are insufficient to make MedCure whole; and c) a capped liquidated damages provision (not a full tort remedy) of up to 6 months' fees if a catastrophic outage impacts 2+ regulated production services for >8 hours.

Key asks:
- Can Redwood accept a staged holdback (we proposed the percentages) rather than immediate escrow?
- Can you provide a proposed cure timetable for each tranche (we suggested a 14-day cure for tranche 1, 30-day cure for tranche 2)?
- Any objections to the 6-month capped LD for catastrophic events?

We'd like to resolve this ahead of the executive procurement review on Nov 10. I've cc'd MedCure procurement for visibility.

Regards,
Lina Park
Farrington LLP (external counsel)
On behalf of MedCure, Inc

Lina — thanks for the note and the annotated doc. Appreciate the detail and the timeline.

Quick response while I loop in legal and our commercial lead (Marissa) and product (Karthik):
- We are open to a staged financial holdback structure versus immediate escrow, but need to nail the operational triggers and cure mechanics so it's not a de facto termination on short incidents.
- 14/30-day cure windows look aggressive for infra-level fixes depending on root cause; we may propose a graduated cure period tied to the severity and root-cause class (e.g., network/provider edge vs. product bug).
- The 6-month capped LD for "catastrophic" events will require a precise definition (what counts as regulated service impact; which metrics; how to measure concurrent service impact).

I'll internalize options with Marissa and Karthik and send a counterproposal by EOD Monday Nov 2 with specific language and a proposed schedule PDF.

— Jonas
VP, Sales (Redwood Inference)

Jonas / Karthik,

Reviewing Lina's asks. High-level thoughts:
- Commercial: staged holdbacks are acceptable if we can define a remediation ladder and a maximum cumulative exposure we can cap in the SOW (we should avoid an open-ended cash exposure). Suggest cap at 3 months' fees total across all tranches.
- Ops/Product: need precise detection rules. We can propose severity definitions tied to availability windows and per-service impact counts. For SRE response, 45 minutes is reasonable for detection but root-cause may justify longer cure in some cases (e.g., cloud provider incident).
- Legal: liquidated damages up to 6 months is high; recommend countering to 3 months with explicit carveouts for force majeure and provider-level incidents.

I'll draft proposed language for: a) staggered holdback percentages; b) cure windows that expand if the root cause is with a third-party provider; c) a max cumulative cap and an explicit definition of catastrophic outage.

Also flagging: if MedCure requires unilateral termination after second incident, we should request an optional remediation review period and right to cure within 7 days before termination becomes effective.

Will circulate a redline and an accompanying PDF (Redwood-Proposed-Tranche-Schedule.pdf) by EOD.

Marissa
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood counterproposal: staged tranche schedule + cure timetable

Lina / MedCure team —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is Redwood's counterproposal (see PDF: Redwood-Proposed-Tranche-Schedule.pdf) and a short summary below. We tried to preserve MedCure's risk objectives while keeping liability bounded and operationally measurable.

Summary of our counterproposal:
- Tranches and holdbacks: 8% holdback (month 1), 16% holdback (month 3), 24% holdback (month 6). Cumulative cap: 3 months' fees across all tranches.
- Incident triggers: Severity-1 incident is defined as a complete service unavailability for one or more production services that impacts >5% of users or >2 regulated production services concurrently.
- Cure timetable: 14-day cure for tranche 1 (root-cause remediation plan + mitigation implemented); 30-day cure for tranche 2; 45-day cure for tranche 3. If root cause is a third-party cloud provider or backbone outage, cure periods extend by the duration of the provider incident (documented via provider status page) but stay subject to the cumulative cap.
- Termination right: unilateral termination only available after two consecutive qualifying Severity-1 incidents where Redwood fails to cure within the applicable cure period and cumulative fees paid as credits/holdbacks do not make MedCure whole. Prior to termination, parties must undergo a 7-day remediation review attempt.
- Liquidated damages: capped at 3 months' fees for catastrophic outages (we removed open-ended tort exposure). Exclusions: force majeure, customer misuse, and third-party provider failures outside Redwood control (unless due to Redwood's negligent orchestration).

We believe this balances MedCure's need for meaningful remedies and Redwood's need to limit unpredictable exposure. Please review the attached redline — we can take a quick call tomorrow Nov 3 to walk through any remaining redlines.

Best,
Jonas Weber
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-Proposed-Tranche-Schedule.pdf (proposed language + sample timeline)

Jonas — thanks for the thoughtful counterproposal and the clarity on definitions. MedCure procurement and legal have reviewed and are generally amenable to the following with one change request:

- Accept the staged holdback percentages and the 3-month cumulative cap.
- Accept the graduated cure windows provided the remediation review period before termination remains 10 business days instead of 7 (they want slightly more runway).
- Regarding third-party provider extension: MedCure wants a binding requirement that Redwood document mitigation steps taken when the root cause is a provider failure (they want auditability).
- Liquidated damages: MedCure will accept 3 months' cap if we can add an explicit definition of "catastrophic outage" to the SOW and a mutually-agreed post-mortem remediation plan requirement within 30 days.

We've attached the annotated doc with the acceptance and the one change (MedCure-Counterterms-annotated.docx). If Redwood can accept the 10 business day remediation review and the auditability requirement, procurement is comfortable moving to exec approval. Can we get a final redline by EOD Wed Nov 4?

If helpful, we can set a 30-minute call tomorrow (Nov 4) to finalize language.
